feature: Customer Portal v2 -- Reference -> SOPs & Runbooks (/portal-v2/sops), WIRED TO REAL DATA. Part 6 built the hub and its three sub-views (library / execution queue / execution history, each a real linkable URL) against the design's own fixtures in sopHubData.ts. This manifest covers the pass that replaced those fixtures with GET /api/portal/sops and GET /api/portal/sop-runs (api-server routes/portal-sops.ts) -- customer-scoped reads over msp_sops + msp_sop_runs, requireRole(CustomerUser), scope from the authenticated JWT only. So it asserts two things the UI-only version could not: that the endpoints are real, correctly scoped and role-gated, and that the DOM shows what THEY returned rather than what the fixture used to say. The four sop-* category pages are the prototype's `sopCategories` (shell 8789), which the design renders through its generic placeholder branch (shell 6500-6507) and which carry no tenant data at all -- covered here as routes, unchanged by the wiring pass.
notes: THE LOGIN BLOCK IS NOT OPTIONAL. /portal-v2/* sits behind ProtectedRoute; a probe that skips the five login steps hits the login screen and every assertion fails for a reason unrelated to the page.

UI ROUTE SHAPE: msp-portal's outer WouterRouter has base '/portal' and SlugScope nests a second router at '/{slug}', so the real URL is /portal/{slug}/portal-v2/sops. App.tsx declares the four /sops/<category> routes BEFORE '/sops/:view' (the queue/audit param) and both before '/portal-v2/:pillar' so nothing is swallowed.
shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree; deploy before running.

PERSISTED-SESSION FLAKE (known): when WebView2 is already authed, the two input steps against #email/#password can fail while the rest runs green because auth persists. N-2 of N with only those two red is a PASS for the feature.

ROLE FLOOR IS HIGHER HERE THAN ON SIBLING PORTAL-V2 PAGES, ON PURPOSE. portal-runbooks.ts / portal-change-control.ts / portal-remediation-tracker.ts all sit at requireRole('Assessment'); these two routes sit at requireRole('CustomerUser'), because the SOP library is the MSP's own procedure documentation plus whatever the customer's team wrote, which is not prospect-tier content. A1 asserts the auth gate and A2 pins the testbed account's role, so if TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL is ever moved to an Assessment-tier account this manifest fails LOUDLY at A2 with the real role in the failure text, rather than every UI step failing for an unexplained reason. (A stale note on an older manifest claimed this account WAS Assessment-role; verified against the live login response 2026-08-21 -- it is CustomerUser, customerId 1, mspId 1.)

THE LIBRARY IS NOW SEEDED, NOT A SINGLE ROW. A2b calls the dev-origin-gated, self-scoped /admin/testbed/seed-sops, which idempotently upserts 7 realistic SOPs for the caller's own mspId (4 runnable -- a step carrying a real graphEndpoint -- across Identity/Incident-Response/Governance/Data-Protection, and 3 manual). It NEVER deletes, so the original SOP-CUSTOM-592 'Test' row (the lowest id, hence library[0]) survives and A4/A5/S9/S11 still key off it. A3c then AUTHORS a new SOP through the real POST /api/portal/sops (201, manual + non-runnable by construction) and A3d proves it is in the library. Because authoring adds a row per run, the count-pinned assertions were removed: S6 asserts a seeded TITLE in the DOM, S7 asserts the count readout is present rather than an exact number, and S8c explicitly selects the 'Test' row so the detail assertions stay deterministic. S20/S24 still key off the 'Test' SOP and the empty msp_sop_runs queue.

PROVING THE FIXTURES ARE ACTUALLY GONE is half the point, so it is asserted twice over: A3 and A8 use expect.containsNone on the real response bodies, and S10/S25 assert the fixture's own index and queue testids are ABSENT from the DOM. A page still reading sopHubData would pass every positive assertion below and fail these.

THE HOLD BANNER IS NOT ASSERTED IN THE DOM, on purpose. It now derives from the real hold-window summary on GET /api/portal/runbooks (the source Active Runbooks owns), so whether it renders at all depends on live hold state for this tenant -- asserting it present would be asserting today's hold windows, and asserting it absent would break the moment a window opens. A9 asserts the SOURCE endpoint instead, which is the part this pass is responsible for.
ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD.

apiTests.name: A1 -- the SOP library refuses an unauthenticated caller.
SETUP -- log in as the designated TESTBED account; extract the bearer.
A2 -- the testbed account clears the CustomerUser floor these routes require. See the ROLE FLOOR note.
A2b -- SEED the SOP library so the hub has real content. Dev-origin gated + self-scoped to the caller's own mspId; idempotent upsert of 7 SOPs (never a delete), so it is safe to re-run.
A3 -- GET /api/portal/sops returns THIS tenant's real library, now carrying the seeded content and still none of the retired fixture content.
